messages:
Maya Patel: proposing a compact 'mini-rollout killchain' for small feature rollouts (3-10% traffic). goal: low-friction, auditable auto-fallbacks + quick human re-entry.

Priya Singh: what are the concrete failure modes we want to auto-handle?

Maya Patel: quick list: 1) sudden 5xx surge 2) memory OOM in pods 3) request queue growth 4) catastrophic latency spike at p99. those should be circuit-breakers.

Kenji Watanabe (Router): we need an atomic route switch API. if auto-fallback fires, router should switch traffic in one RPC and emit an audit event. will need SDK support.

Jordan (SRE): detection windows:
- immediate emergency: 45-90s rolling window for 5xx rate > threshold OR queue_length > Y -> auto-fallback
- observational: 10-20m window for model-quality regressions (eval alerts) -> page only

Sam Lee: launch gating I'd push for: canary at 3% for 45m no emergency trips + canary eval pass on the canonical prompt set + QA smoke pass.

Maya Patel: also: auto-fallback actions prioritized: 1) route to cached (if hit rate high enough) 2) swap to lightweight quantized model on same hardware 3) route to older stable model 4) full-disable. default is step 2.

qa-bot: quick note: add a synthetic checker that runs the important prompts every 30s against the canary variant and records divergence score.

Kenji Watanabe (Router): sample flag payload we expect from the flag service (pseudo):
```
flag_name: mini_rollout_killchain
regions: [us-west-2]
percent: 3
fallbacks: ["cache","model-quant-v1","model-stable-v0"]
auto_kill_window: 60s
auto_shrink_ttl: 15m
audit: true
```

Jordan (SRE): monitoring + alerts:
- emergency_alert: rate(5xx[1m]) > 0.025 OR increase(queue_len,1m) > 50 -> run automation hook
- quality_alert: model_regression_score > 0.02 over 15m -> page

Maya Patel: governance: every auto-fallback must create an audit entry with: timestamp, region, triggering_metric, pre_fallback_traffic_pct, post_fallback_destination, request_id_sample. compliance needs that for audits.

Sam Lee: experiments: if variant is part of an active A/B, automation should default to redirecting that cohort to control variant rather than turning the feature off. this preserves experiment integrity.

Priya Singh: operational UX ask: provide an override TTL when reintroducing traffic, and a two-step reintroduce flow (aka two-person approval) with an auto-expire guard.

Kenji Watanabe (Router): implementing route-swap + two-person reintroduce is doable. I can prototype a Slack workflow that logs approvers and calls the router API.

Maya Patel: QA and e2e: QA to run synthetic regression checks and validate fallback correctness. qa-bot to post results into thread automatically.

qa-bot: scheduled: canary-synth-check run -> 0.8% divergence -> PASS

Jordan (SRE): ops detail: expose a dashboard widget showing live canary p50/p99, 5xx rate, and last fallback event with a quick link to the audit record. also emit metric auto_fallbacks_total{reason="5xx",region="us-west-2"}.

Sam Lee: acceptance criteria for promoting to 10%: 2h at baseline for both emergency and quality windows, zero auto-fallbacks, and oncall sign-off.

Maya Patel: owners + timeline:
- Maya: finalize YAML spec + audit schema by Tue
- Kenji: router API + Slack-approval flow prototype by Wed
- Jordan: alert rules + dashboard tile by Thu
- Priya: experiment-aware flow + docs by Thu
- QA: synthetic checks wired and passing by Fri

ops-oncall: will watch first mini rollout and report. set pager and escalate on quality_alert.

Maya Patel: thanks all. I will push the spec and tag this thread. please reply with any missing edge cases.
